learning_objective: 🎯 Put your integration skills to work! Learn how to find the exact area of irregular shapes and regions trapped between curves.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: To find the area under a curve, we imagine cutting it into infinitely thin vertical or horizontal rectangular strips, and then we use integration to add all those tiny areas together.

main_concepts.concept_title: 🚧 Area Bounded by a Curve and an Axis
main_concepts.simple_explanation: If the region sits on the x-axis, we integrate the function $y$ with respect to $x$ ($ydx$). If it clings to the y-axis, we integrate the function $x$ with respect to $y$ ($xdy$).
When a region is trapped between a 'top' curve and a 'bottom' curve, you simply integrate the (Top Function - Bottom Function) between their points of intersection.

fun_activity.title: 🍕 The Pizza Slice Integral
fun_activity.instructions: Draw a perfect circle $x^2 + y^2 = 16$ on graph paper. This circle has a radius of 4. Use a definite integral from 0 to 4 to find the area of the first quadrant (one slice), then multiply by 4 to see if it matches the standard $\pi r^2$ formula!

exam_tips: 📌 ALWAYS draw a rough sketch of the curves before solving. You will lose marks if you don't show the graph and shade the required bounded region.
📌 Find the points of intersection algebraically (by solving the two curve equations simultaneously) before setting your integral limits.
📌 If the area dips below the x-axis, the integral will be negative. Put absolute value bars around it ($|Area|$) because actual physical area cannot be negative!
quick_recap: ⭐ Integration adds up infinite tiny rectangles to find total area.
⭐ Always identify whether it is easier to use vertical strips ($dx$) or horizontal strips ($dy$).
⭐ Area = Integral of (Upper Curve - Lower Curve).
